text:
incident-bot: ALERT DNS failures + high tail latency for EU customers to api.redwood-inference.com. Observed spike in DNS NXDOMAIN/timeout and client-side timeouts starting 02:09 UTC. Auto-page to on-call.
maya_sre: I'm on call. Paging @tom_netops and @oliver_platform. First check: are Route53 / cloud DNS edits in the last hour? :mag_right:
tom_netops: Not from us. No config changes in infra repo. Seeing increased 530s from edge nodes when resolving api.redwood-inference.com — dig from eu-west edge returns intermittent no answer. Doing a quick dig:
```
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood-inference.com
(occasionally empty)
$ dig +trace api.redwood-inference.com
;; global LB responds but region endpoints missing in some NS responses
```
oliver_platform: Cloud provider console shows partial outage in eu-west-1 DNS resolver cluster at ~02:05 UTC, with elevated latencies. Provider incident ID CL-9982. They say resolution in progress.
nina_support: Customer impact: multiple support tickets from EU customers (tickets #4001, #4002). Symptoms: client-side DNS timeouts causing SDK to fail before retry logic. One customer reported 5 retries failed at 02:12 UTC.
emma_pm: We should post a status page note quickly and advise customers to retry. Drafting now.
cloud-dns-bot: Provider note: eu-west-1 DNS resolver cluster reported 20% packet loss between 02:03-02:20 UTC. Failover to global resolvers recommended.
maya_sre: Mitigation plan: 1) Force edge nodes to use alternative resolvers (internal forwarders) for affected region; 2) Lower LB weight for eu-west to reduce client sensitivity to DNS; 3) If needed, apply transient DNS record to point to eu-central as emergency fallback.
tom_netops: Starting with edge change. Command to update resolver on edges:
```
ansible-playbook playbooks/dns-forwarder.yml -l edge-eu --extra-vars "resolver=10.10.20.5"
```
tom_netops: rolled out to 20% edges as canary. Metrics show immediate drop in DNS errors for canary nodes.
oliver_platform: Provider says full resolver cluster recovery ETA unknown, they recommend traffic failover. I'll open a support escalation.
cloud-dns-bot: Provider escalation opened: CL-9982-Esc. Contacted ops at 02:25 UTC.
maya_sre: If edge resolver change holds, expand to 100% and then consider LB weight shift. Also add a short TTL override on api records? That is risky.
emma_pm: Status page posted: "We're investigating increased DNS-related errors for EU customers. We're applying mitigations and will provide updates every 30 minutes." :loudspeaker:
nina_support: Customers updated. One large customer asked for immediate rollback to previous DNS alias—can't do DNS rollback, would need traffic shift.
tom_netops: After expanding resolver change, DNS lookup errors dropped ~90% by 02:40 UTC. However, some SDKs cache negative responses and continue failing. Recommend advising customers to restart services or clear DNS cache as temporary workaround.
maya_sre: Good. Next: reduce LB weight for eu-west to 0 over 10 minutes and shift to eu-central to limit client fallback churn. Command:
```
$ lbctl weight set --pool eu-west --weight 0 --duration 10m --author=tom
```
tom_netops: Applying weight shift now. Monitoring.
oliver_platform: Weight shift applied. Observed fewer 5xx at edge and global p95 latency improving.
nina_support: Customers report progressive improvement; two confirmed full recovery after service restarts.
cloud-dns-bot: Provider update: resolver cluster fully recovered at 03:05 UTC, but recommend reviewing why split-horizon responses missed regional endpoints.
maya_sre: Since provider recovered, we will revert edge resolver override and restore LB weights to normal. Plan: 1) revert ansible change; 2) monitor for 15m; 3) follow-up postmortem.
tom_netops: Reverting resolver on edges now. ```ansible-playbook playbooks/dns-forwarder.yml -l edge-eu --extra-vars "resolver=auto"``` Revert done.
oliver_platform: LB weights restored to baseline at 03:12 UTC.
maya_sre: Confirming metrics: DNS NXDOMAINs and client errors back to baseline at 03:18 UTC. Marking incident mitigated.
emma_pm: Status update posted: "Service stabilized at 03:18 UTC. Root cause under investigation: partial DNS resolver cluster failure at provider leading to intermittent missing records for regional endpoints. Postmortem to follow." :white_check_mark:
nina_support: Notified impacted customers and closed immediate tickets; follow-up comms planned.
maya_sre: Initial RCA notes: provider DNS resolver cluster had packet loss, exposing our reliance on region-specific DNS responses and client-side negative caching. Work items:
- Add synthetic DNS monitors from multiple public resolvers and from our edge regions (owner: oliver_platform)
- Implement fallback resolver config in edge agent with faster failover (owner: tom_netops)
- Add customer-facing guidance for clearing negative DNS cache in SDKs (owner: nina_support)
- Add pre-announce checks for any DNS/Zone changes and reduce TTL for critical records (owner: maya_sre)
- Engage provider for post-incident review and SLA review (owner: oliver_platform)
maya_sre: On-call handoff: I'll hand to @tom_netops in 30m. Please keep channel open for postmortem details. Thanks all. :handshake:
